prerequisites: Knowledge of differential and integral calculus
Knowledge of the sum of arithmetic / trigonometric series

learning_outcomes.text: Acquaint students with the representation, processing and analysis of discrete signals and systems (filters) used in communication and control technology.
Use tools for the analysis of discrete periodic and non-periodic signals in the time and frequency domain.
Design discrete systems with required characteristics (by solving differential equations and by z-transform).
Understand sampling and subsequent quantization of continuous signals.
Perform state-space analysis of discrete signals.
Gain knowledge in the field of digital signal processing and their analysis in the time and frequency domain.
Be acquainted with the issues of A/D conversion of continuous signals and analysis of continuous systems in the time and frequency domain.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical apparatus for processing discrete signals
Representation, modelling, classification and description of discrete signals. Discrete signal operations
Basic types of discrete signals (harmonic signals, unit pulse, unit jump, pulse signal, triangular signal)
Discrete systems in the time domain, block representation, properties of systems, FIR and IIR systems
Description of discrete systems using differential equations and their solutions
Tools for analysis of discrete periodic signals in the frequency domain (DTFS)
Tools for analysis of discrete non-periodic signals in the frequency domain (DTFT)
Discrete Fourier transform, fast computational algorithms (FFT)
Z-transformation II. (Z-transformation of significant signals, inverse Z-transformation)
Determination of frequency characteristics of discrete systems
Sampling of continuous signals I. (types of sampling), conditions and effects of sampling in the time and frequency domain
Sampling of continuous signals II. (quantization, effects of quantization, A / D converters, SQNR)
assessment_rules: Attendance rate of at least 80% and completion of all homework assignments are prerequisites for successful completion. Each homework assignment is marked with a maximum of 3 points and must be corrected if wrong; all must be turned in. The oral exam consists of three questions, each scoring 1 point, with a minimum of 0.5 points required for each question. The final grade is based on a score table ranging from A (3-2.7 points) to F (<1.5 points).
degree: Bachelor's programme, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Informatics - courses in English
